      - text: DISCRETE AND APPLIED MATHEMATICS FINANCIAL MATHEMATICS AND MODELLING
      - heading "Profit, Loss, Markup and Margin" [level=1]
      - paragraph: "Objective: Connect cost, selling price, profit/loss, markup and margin in a pricing model."
      - text: Level Intermediate-Advanced Lab Interactive Modelling Skill Business Mathematics Time 6-10 min
      - navigation:
        - button "Interact"
        - button "Learn"
        - button "Worked Example"
        - button "Formula"
        - button "Practice"
      - heading "MANIPULATE THE MODEL" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Drag the selling price to see how profit, loss, markup and margin change.
      - complementary: Drag the orange point or adjust the slider.
      - main:
        - img "Cost and selling price model": Cost ₹800 Selling Price ₹1,100 Price (₹)
        - text: Selling price (₹)
        - strong: 1,100
        - text: "400"
        - slider "Selling price slider": "1100"
        - text: 2,000
        - button "Show as loss"
        - button "Show as profit"
      - complementary:
        - heading "CURRENT RESULTS" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Profit (₹) +300
        - paragraph: Markup (% of cost) 37.50%
        - paragraph: Margin (% of selling price) 27.27%
        - text: Cost ₹800 Selling price ₹1,100 Profit ₹300
        - complementary: Markup compares profit to cost. Margin compares profit to selling price.
      - article:
        - heading "NOTICE THE PATTERN" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Try a few selling prices.
        - table:
          - rowgroup:
            - row "Selling Price (₹) Profit (₹) Markup (%) Margin (%)":
              - columnheader "Selling Price (₹)"
              - columnheader "Profit (₹)"
              - columnheader "Markup (%)"
              - columnheader "Margin (%)"
          - rowgroup:
            - row "600 −200 −25.00% −33.33%":
              - cell "600"
              - cell "−200"
              - cell "−25.00%"
              - cell "−33.33%"
            - row "800 +0 0.00% 0.00%":
              - cell "800"
              - cell "+0"
              - cell "0.00%"
              - cell "0.00%"
            - row "1,100 +300 37.50% 27.27%":
              - cell "1,100"
              - cell "+300"
              - cell "37.50%"
              - cell "27.27%"
            - row "1,400 +600 75.00% 42.86%":
              - cell "1,400"
              - cell "+600"
              - cell "75.00%"
              - cell "42.86%"
            - row "1,700 +900 112.50% 52.94%":
              - cell "1,700"
              - cell "+900"
              - cell "112.50%"
              - cell "52.94%"
        - complementary: "Notice: Margin is always smaller (in absolute value) than markup for the same profit or loss."
      - article:
        - heading "UNDERSTAND THE RULE" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Key definitions Let C be cost, S be selling price, and P = S − C.
        - strong: "Profit (₹): P = S − C"
        - strong: "Markup (% of cost): 100 × P/C"
        - strong: "Margin (% of selling price): 100 × P/S"
        - paragraph: "Important: Margin < Markup when P > 0."
      - article:
        - heading "WORKED EXAMPLE" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Cost = ₹800, Selling price = ₹1,400
        - text: Profit P = 1,400 − 800 = ₹600 Markup 100 × 600/800 = 75% Margin 100 × 600/1,400 = 42.86%
        - complementary:
          - img
          - text: "Check: Margin < Markup."
      - article:
        - heading "KEY RULE / DEFINITION" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Profit, Markup and Margin
        - strong: P = S − C
        - strong: 100 × (S − C)/C
        - strong: 100 × (S − C)/S
        - complementary: Use markup to compare against cost. Use margin to compare against selling price.
      - article:
        - heading "COMMON MISCONCEPTION" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Markup is not the same as Margin.
        - text: Cost ₹800 → +₹300 → Selling Price ₹1,100
        - paragraph: Markup = 37.50% of cost Margin = 27.27% of selling price
        - complementary: Don't say “37.5% margin.” That would be 37.5% of selling price, not of cost.
      - article:
        - heading "TRY THIS CHALLENGE" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Cost = ₹950. You sell the item at a 20% markup.
        - paragraph: What are the selling price, profit and margin?
